newsitem.title: USA: Drug kingpin Garcia Abrego to be sentenced.
newsitem.headline: Drug kingpin Garcia Abrego to be sentenced.

text.p: Drug kingpin Juan Garcia Abrego was set to be sentenced on Friday following his conviction in October on charges that he smuggled huge quantities of cocaine into the United States.

U.S. District Judge Ewing Werlein was expected to follow federal sentencing guidelines and hand down a life sentence without parole for Garcia Abrego, who was found guilty of all 22 counts against him, including drug-trafficking, money laundering and bribery. He could also be ordered to forfeit up to $350 million in illicit proceeds.

Garcia Abrego, 52, was once one of Mexico's most powerful druglords. U.S. drug agents said at one time his Gulf cartel shipped up to a third of the cocaine consumed in the United States from his base in northern Mexico.
He became the object of an international manhunt when the FBI put him on its 10 Most Wanted list and was captured Jan. 14, 1996, by Mexican agents in the northern Mexico city of Monterrey.
Garcia Abrego, who was born in south Texas, was brought to Houston for trial on U.S. indictments.

U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno hailed his conviction on Oct. 16 as a major victory in the war on drugs, saying it would make U.S. streets safer. But officials say the Gulf cartel remains remains one of Mexico's most powerful drug organisations.
Defence attorney Tony Canales has said he would file an appeal of the conviction following sentencing.
